title: MASLD protection by STAT5-regulated transcription factors
text:
Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) is more prevalent in men, compared to pre-
menopausal women. Preclinical studies are proposed to elucidate underlying molecular mechanisms for how
growth hormone (GH) protects hepatocytes within the female liver from excess fat accumulation and damage,
and for how GH alters hepatocyte communication with other liver cell types to slow disease progression. The
fundamental new knowledge gained in the fields of GH action, sex differences in liver biology, and MASLD
development have real potential to unveil novel therapeutic strategies and druggable targets to treat this
devastating disease, that has become the leading cause of chronic liver failure.

title: Comprehensive Genomic Integrity Assessment for Allogenic Cell Therapies using Genomic proximity mapping
text:
Cell therapies, especial those derived from stem cells can harbor mutations that could lead to cancer
following transplantation. To reduce the likelihood of this complication, we propose the development of a
platform that allows cell therapy developers to rapidly and efficiently determine if cells used to create
therapeutic products have any such cancer-causing mutations.

title: Cerium oxide nanoparticles for CT imaging and catalytic therapeutic intervention in inflammatory bowel disease
text:
Inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) is a serious condition that adversely affects millions of American.
Improvements are needed in the imaging and treatment methods for this disease. We hypothesize that cerium
oxide nanoparticles can address both of these needs and thereby result in better lives for people afflicted by
IBD.

title: ACE and myeloid cell metabolism
text:
The increased expression of angiotensin converting enzyme (ACE) enhances the immune
function of macrophages and neutrophils by altering their metabolism and increasing cell
production of ATP. This proposal is to investigate exactly how ACE modifies myeloid cell
metabolism to learn how to increase myeloid cell function in treating human infection, malignancy
and other diseases.

title: The effects of HIV-associated extracellular vesicles on mitochondrial dysfunction in brain microvessels
text:
Despite the efficacy of combined antiretroviral therapy (cART), the development of HIV-1 associated
neurocognitive disorders (HAND) is a serious clinical complication in AIDS patients. The mechanisms
underlying HAND are underdeveloped, and the current cART regimens are insufficient to inhibit the
progression of HAND. We propose to elucidate the role of extracellular vesicles (EVs) on brain microvascular
endothelial mitochondria in the development of HAND and evaluate the clinically tested mesenchymal stem
cell-derived EVs to prevent neuropathogenesis in the HIV-1 infected humanized mice model.

title: Mechanisms of Hand2-mediated cell migration in mesothelia
text:
Mesothelia are a crucial support tissue, essential for proper organ development, homeostasis, and
immune response. Despite its importance, the molecular and regulatory control of mesothelial cell migration and
its roles in organ formation are unexplored. This will be the focus of my investigations and my results will advance
our understanding of body plan organization, how organ-associated mesothelia support organogenesis and
homeostasis, and how developmental gene regulatory mechanisms are reactivated in disease.

title: Sex Specific Differences in the Remodeling of a Biopolymer Based Tissue Engineered Vascular Graft
text:
Coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG) procedures have up to a 42.8% failure rate over ten years, with post-
menopausal women having the worst outcomes of all vascular graft recipients. As the field moves to develop
tissue-engineered vascular grafts (TEVGs) to be used in CABG procedures, sex-specific remodeling of these
conduits is not well characterized despite clinical evidence of sex-specific failure modes. The proposed research
will investigate both tissue scale and cellular differences in remodeling between different sexes for compliance-
matched TEVGs in vivo using male, female, and post-menopausal female rats to elucidate the role of estrogen
in successful vascular graft integration.

title: Alterations in cyclic AMP signaling in response to immune and drug pressure
text:
Project 2 – Narrative
Tuberculosis (TB) is a leading global cause of death and remains difficult to treat due to the ability of
Mycobacterium tuberculosis to survive within host immune cells and tolerate antibiotics. This project investigates
how Mtb uses cyclic AMP (cAMP) signaling to adapt to the host environment and resist therapy, with the goal of
identifying new therapeutic strategies targeting cAMP metabolism. Understanding how naturally occurring
mutations affect this pathway will help bridge bacterial genetics with drug development and improve treatment
outcomes.

title: Mechanisms of nuclear morphology regulation
text:
Nuclear morphology is often deregulated in cancer cells, many cancers are diagnosed and
staged based on graded increases in nuclear size, and little is known about the causes or effects of nuclear
morphology changes in cancer. We will identify regulators of nuclear size and shape, elucidate mechanisms of
nuclear morphology regulation, and use this information to investigate how nuclear morphology affects
embryonic development, cell differentiation, and carcinogenesis, shedding light on novel approaches and
targets for the diagnosis and treatment of cancer. Aberrant nuclear morphology in cancer might be necessary
for cell homeostasis and viability, so therapeutic manipulation of nuclear morphology could provide a means to
selectively target and kill only affected cells.

title: preclinical optimization of BCMA directed T cell therapy
text:
T-cell directed therapies are the most exciting recent advances in treatment of patients, but after the initial
response patients inevitably relapse to this disease and myeloma remains incurable. We will credential a
mouse model for developing novel combinations of drugs with T-cell directed treatments which will allow for
their rapid clinical development. These studies will likely inform clinical practice on how combine standard of
care agents with immunotherapy.

title: Proteolysis in Hereditary Neutropenia
text:
This project investigates the mechanism of ELANE-associated congenital neutropenia, a life-threatening
disorder that predisposes to infection and leukemia. Using human stem cell models, it will dissect the roles of
neutrophil elastase, related proteases, and their substrates in disrupting granulopoiesis. In addition to identifying
strategies to restore neutrophil production and immune function, these studies will elucidate fundamental
principles of blood cell development with broad relevance to both inherited and acquired forms of neutropenia.

title: Remote ischemic preconditioning for renal and cardiac protection in congestive heart failure (RICH) trial
text:
Contrast-associated acute kidney injury occurs frequently after coronary angiography and percutaneous
coronary intervention in patients with heart failure with reduced left ventricular ejection fraction. Although,
periprocedural administration of intravenous fluid, has been the standard intervention to prevent contrast-
associated acute kidney injury, patients with congestive heart failure may not tolerate intravenous fluid.
Unfortunately, there is no alternative therapy to prevent contrast-associated acute kidney injury in patients
with congestive heart failure. This project will determine the effect of remote ischemic preconditioning on
contrast-associated acute kidney injury in Veterans with congestive heart failure with reduced left
ventricular ejection fraction who cannot tolerate intravenous fluid. It will characterize the effect of remote
ischemic preconditioning on functional capacity and major adverse kidney events in Veterans with
congestive heart failure with reduced left ventricular ejection fraction undergoing coronary angiography.

title: High throughput sample delivery method for time resolved studies of enzyme reactions with X-ray and complementary techniques
text:
The X-ray Free Electron Laser (XFEL) allows for structural determination of enzyme-substrate/drug
interactions at room temperature under functional conditions, and promises to be a revolutionary new tool for
studies in structural biology and the biomedical sciences. Today such studies are nevertheless often limited due
to the absence of methods to trigger/synchronize the enzymatic reaction or the high sample consumption rates
of existing sample delivery systems, as the sample needs to be replenished at the high repetition rate of the X-
ray laser pulses. We will develop sample delivery mechanisms that ensure precise control of the sample
environment (temperature, pressure, gas environment) while allowing to work with scarce samples and triggering
a wide variety of reactions, in particular, by chemical mixing, temperature jump, or electrochemical activation,
with parallel multimodal detection schemes and integrate these with existing experimental stations at various
user facilities.

title: Harvard University Center for AIDS Research
text: The Harvard University CFAR (HU CFAR) provides the infrastructure to coordinate, support and add value to Harvard investigators’cutting-edge multidisciplinary HIV research programs and to forge new collaborations and synergies. The HU CFAR pursues innovative initiatives to address critical HIV-related research priorities and train the next generation of HIV researchers. By leveraging the exceptional strengths of Harvard and its institutional support, the HU CFAR promises to continue to provide major leadership in the global effort to prevent and treat HIV.

title: Proteotoxic Metabolites in Genome Instability and Disease
text:
This project will define mechanisms of proteotoxicity underlying the genome instability phenotypes caused by
reactive aldehydes that accumulate in cancers and diverse other age-related diseases. Insights from its
findings will identify useful targets for the prevention and management of aldehyde-related diseases and may
provide novel biomarkers of proteotoxicity and genome instability for biomonitoring, early diagnosis, and risk
stratification.

title: Optimized Targeting of FLT3 and Menin in KMT2A-R ALL toOvercome Immunotherapeutic Resistance
text:
KMT2A rearrangements occur in >75% of infants (less than one year of age) diagnosed with B-lymphoblastic
leukemia (ALL) and in 10% of older children and adults; patients with KMT2A-rearranged ALL across the age
spectrum have high rates of chemotherapy resistance that results in inferior clinical outcomes. Chimeric antigen
receptor (CAR) T cells and epigenetic-modulating drugs (eg, hypomethylating chemotherapy agents, DOT1L
inhibitors, menin inhibitors) have activity against these leukemias, but emergence of distinct mechanisms of
resistance to each of these therapies commonly occurs. In this proposal, we propose to develop best-in-class
FLT3 CAR T cell immunotherapies via rigorous optimization of novel FLT3 binder constructs and to investigate
combinatorial CAR T cell immunotherapy strategies co-targeting CD19 or FLT3 antigens with menin inhibition in
vitro and in vivo using sophisticated patient-relevant preclinical models with an overarching goal of overcoming
KMT2A-rearranged ALL treatment resistance via alternative FLT3 antigen immunotherapeutic targeting and
epigenetic modulation to augment CAR T cell fitness.

title: Harnessing the therapeutic potential of histotripsy focused ultrasound-induced immunogenic cancer cell death
text:
We have determined that histotripsy, a novel technology that ablates tumors precisely and non-invasively using
high intensity ultrasound waves, triggers a sequence of cell death events in treated and distant, untreated tumors
that culminate in a systemic anti-tumor immune response that is stronger than that generated by existing modes
of tumor ablation. We will examine three distinct cellular events that follow histotripsy ablation – the exposure of
contents hidden inside tumor cells, the triggering of inflammatory cancer cell suicide of cancer cells, and immune
cell-driven cancer cell death – to determine the extent to which these unique events mechanistically drive the
phenomenon of histotripsy immunostimulation. By understanding these events and testing preclincal strategies
to harness and maximize them, we hope to establish a scientific foundation for implementing histotripsy tumor
ablation as a means of maximizing the impact of cancer immunotherapy.

title: Novel NIR probes for multiplexed imaging of cancer
text:
This proposal aims to develop a novel class of near-infrared (NIR) bioimaging probes based on hybrid
AgNCs@DNA@NANP nanostructures. By combining the high emissivity of silver nanoclusters (AgNCs) with
the multifunctionality of nucleic acid nanoparticles (NANPs), we will create stable, cost-effective, and
biocompatible probes. These probes will enhance the efficiency of cytoreductive therapy for aggressive
ovarian cancer while improving diagnosis and prognosis.

title: Enhanced Sampling of Intracellular Protein Interactions with G-Protein-Coupled Receptors
text:
The objective of this project is to develop a novel computational method that integrates enhanced sampling and
Deep Learning to calculate the lifetime and dissociation kinetics of protein complexes efficiently. We will apply it
to predict changes in the dissociation kinetics and lifetime of adenosine and muscarinic G-protein-coupled
receptor-G protein/arrestin complexes upon binding of allosteric modulators and biased agonists, and validate
our simulation predictions in collaborative experiments. This will greatly facilitate rational design of selective
therapeutic drugs of target receptors.

title: Dissecting neural circuits regulating sleep fragmentation in Parkinson’s disease
text:
Parkinson’s disease is a common neurodegenerative disease that produces debilitating motor and non-motor
symptoms, including sleep disturbances. Despite our increased understanding of the mechanisms of motor
symptoms in Parkinson’s disease, the mechanisms underlying sleep disturbances are poorly understood, which
has limited our ability to develop targeted therapeutics to treat these disabling sleep symptoms. The goal of this
proposal is to study sleep state transitions in a mouse model of Parkinson’s disease.
